query: Equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its quaternary and ternary subsets provide 16 candidate alloys, nine of which are single-phase FCC after thermomechanical processing. Early reports associated increasing constituent count with greater strength, but that simple relationship is no longer generally accepted. Despite extensive experimental and theoretical investigation, the origins of differences in deformation and failure behavior remain unresolved; practical interpretation must also account for constituent cost and overall cost-performance balance. What testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs these mechanical-property differences and why? Define a controlled investigation, the observations predicted relative to the equiatomic quinary baseline, the limits within which the hypothesis should apply, the prior evidence supporting it, and an observation that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The mechanical-property differences in equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its subsets are governed by the local lattice distortion induced by atomic size mismatch, which affects dislocation motion and, consequently, strength and ductility.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni high-entropy alloy and its quaternary and ternary subsets, processed to a single-phase FCC structure.
generation.intervention: Systematic variation of constituent elements to create alloys with different levels of atomic size mismatch, while maintaining single-phase FCC structure through thermomechanical processing.
generation.conditions: Room temperature mechanical testing under uniaxial tension or compression, with consistent processing history to ensure comparable microstructures.
generation.structural_mediator: Local lattice distortion quantified by atomic size mismatch and its effect on dislocation motion.
generation.mechanism: Increased atomic size mismatch leads to greater local lattice distortion, which impedes dislocation motion and increases strength but may reduce ductility due to localized stress concentrations.
generation.predicted_outcome: Alloys with higher atomic size mismatch will exhibit increased yield strength and reduced ductility relative to the equiatomic quinary baseline.
generation.baseline: Mechanical properties of the equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy.
generation.boundary: Hypothesis applies to single-phase FCC alloys derived from the Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni system with atomic size mismatch values within the range that maintains FCC stability.
generation.uncertainty: The extent to which atomic size mismatch alone governs mechanical properties is uncertain, as other factors like electronic structure and short-range ordering may also contribute.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of alloys with controlled variations in atomic size mismatch by substituting elements of different atomic radii into the Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni system, ensuring single-phase FCC structure through thermomechanical processing. Perform uniaxial tensile tests to measure yield strength and ductility.
measurements: Atomic size mismatch (calculated from atomic radii)
Microstructural analysis to confirm single-phase FCC structure
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If alloys with higher atomic size mismatch do not show a consistent trend of increased yield strength and reduced ductility compared to the equiatomic quinary baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.
